gauntlet: question
A fits because the existing resolver already owns this view's settings. `settings/resolver.ts:12` defines the defaults, and the traced data path delivers resolved values to `ui/report-view.ts:30`. Every existing setting already uses that path. A view-local object would add a second settings source beside the one that owns them. Defaults and precedence would then live in two places that could drift apart.

The resolver will own the new setting. The open choice is what the setting does when you switch workspaces, since the reported problem is filters carrying over and hiding rows. What should happen to active report filters on a workspace change?
A) reset filters by default, with the setting letting a user keep them
B) keep filters by default (today's behavior), with the setting letting a user opt into reset
C) other - name it
Recommendation: A - the reported harm is rows hidden in the new workspace, so the default should prevent it. Users who want to carry filters across workspaces can still turn that on.

The new setting can follow that traced path without introducing a second settings object or a synchronization responsibility in the view. I’ll carry your choice forward as the ownership decision; it does not yet decide filter-reset behavior.

What should the new setting’s default behavior be when switching workspaces?
A) Clear active report filters so rows in the new workspace are not hidden by the previous workspace’s filters.
B) Preserve active report filters, keeping today’s behavior unless the user enables resetting.
C) Other - name the desired behavior.
Recommendation: A - it addresses the hidden-row problem you described by default.
